passages.text: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valor; he was the son of a prostitute, and Gilead was his father.
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a Gileadite.
He was a mighty man of valor.
His mother was a prostitute.
Gilead was his father.
passages.original: וְיִפְתָּ֣ח הַגִּלְעָדִ֗י הָיָה֙ גִּבּ֣וֹר חַ֔יִל וְה֖וּא בֶּן־ אִשָּׁ֣ה זוֹנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד גִּלְעָ֖ד אֶת־ יִפְתָּֽח׃

passages.text: And Gilead’s wife bore him sons who grew up, drove Jephthah out, and said to him, “You shall have no inheritance in our father’s house, because you are the son of another woman.”
passages.sermon:
Gilead’s wife gave birth to sons for him.
These sons grew up.
They drove Jephthah out.
They said to Jephthah, “You will not inherit in our father’s house.
You are the son of another woman.”
passages.original: וַתֵּ֧לֶד אֵֽשֶׁת־ גִּלְעָ֛ד ל֖וֹ בָּנִ֑ים וַיִּגְדְּל֨וּ בְֽנֵי־ הָאִשָּׁ֜ה וַיְגָרְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־ יִפְתָּ֗ח וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ לֹֽא־ תִנְחַ֣ל בְּבֵית־ אָבִ֔ינוּ כִּ֛י בֶּן־ אִשָּׁ֥ה אַחֶ֖רֶת אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: So Jephthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob, where worthless men gathered around him and traveled with him.
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a mighty man of valor.
He was the son of a prostitute.
Gilead was his father.
Jephthah’s brothers drove him away.
Jephthah fled from his brothers.
He went to the land of Tob.
Worthless men gathered around Jephthah.
These men traveled with him.
passages.original: וַיִּבְרַ֤ח יִפְתָּח֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י אֶחָ֔יו וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּאֶ֣רֶץ ט֑וֹב וַיִּֽתְלַקְּט֤וּ אֶל־ יִפְתָּח֙ אֲנָשִׁ֣ים רֵיקִ֔ים וַיֵּצְא֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: Some time later, when the Ammonites fought against Israel and made war with them, the elders of Gilead went to get Jephthah from the land of Tob.
passages.sermon:
The Ammonites attacked Israel.
They fought against Israel.
This happened some time later.
The elders of Gilead saw this trouble.
They went to the land of Tob.
They went there to get Jephthah.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֖י מִיָּמִ֑ים וַיִּלָּחֲמ֥וּ בְנֵֽי־ עַמּ֖וֹן עִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁר־ נִלְחֲמ֥וּ בְנֵֽי־ עַמּ֖וֹן עִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ זִקְנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֔ד לָקַ֥חַת אֶת־ יִפְתָּ֖ח מֵאֶ֥רֶץ טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: “Come,” they said, “be our commander, so that we can fight against the Ammonites.”
passages.sermon:
The elders of Gilead spoke to Jephthah.
They said, “Come with us.”
They said, “Be our commander.”
They said, “Lead us in battle against the Ammonites.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לְיִפְתָּ֔ח לְכָ֕ה וְהָיִ֥יתָה לָּ֖נוּ לְקָצִ֑ין וְנִֽלָּחֲמָ֖ה בִּבְנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Jephthah replied to the elders of Gilead, “Did you not hate me and expel me from my father’s house? Why then have you come to me now, when you are in distress?”
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a man from Gilead.
The elders of Gilead had once hated Jephthah.
They had driven Jephthah out of his father’s house.
Jephthah spoke to the elders of Gilead.
He said, “You hated me.”
He said, “You sent me away from my father’s house.”
He asked, “Why do you come to me now?”
He asked, “Why do you come when you are in trouble?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִפְתָּח֙ לְזִקְנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֔ד הֲלֹ֤א אַתֶּם֙ שְׂנֵאתֶ֣ם אוֹתִ֔י וַתְּגָרְשׁ֖וּנִי מִבֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑י וּמַדּ֜וּעַ בָּאתֶ֤ם אֵלַי֙ עַ֔תָּה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צַ֥ר לָכֶֽם׃

passages.text: They answered Jephthah, “This is why we now turn to you, that you may go with us, fight the Ammonites, and become leader over all of us who live in Gilead.”
passages.sermon:
The elders of Gilead spoke to Jephthah.
They said, “We have come back to you now.
We want you to go with us.
We want you to fight against the Ammonites with us.
We want you to become our leader.
You will be leader over everyone who lives in Gilead.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ זִקְנֵ֨י גִלְעָ֜ד אֶל־ יִפְתָּ֗ח לָכֵן֙ עַתָּה֙ שַׁ֣בְנוּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְהָלַכְתָּ֣ עִמָּ֔נוּ וְנִלְחַמְתָּ֖ בִּבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן וְהָיִ֤יתָ לָּ֙נוּ֙ לְרֹ֔אשׁ לְכֹ֖ל יֹשְׁבֵ֥י גִלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: But Jephthah asked them, “If you take me back to fight the Ammonites and the LORD gives them to me, will I really be your leader?”
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a man from Gilead.
The elders of Gilead had come to Jephthah.
Jephthah spoke to the elders of Gilead.
He said, “If you bring me back to fight against the Ammonites,
and if the LORD gives the Ammonites into my hand,
will I truly become your leader?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִפְתָּ֜ח אֶל־ זִקְנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֗ד אִם־ מְשִׁיבִ֨ים אַתֶּ֤ם אוֹתִי֙ לְהִלָּחֵם֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וְנָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה אוֹתָ֖ם לְפָנָ֑י אָנֹכִ֕י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לְרֹֽאשׁ׃

passages.text: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “The LORD is our witness if we do not do as you say.”
passages.sermon:
The elders of Gilead spoke to Jephthah.
They said, "The LORD is our witness."
They promised to do exactly as Jephthah said.
They said they would not fail to keep his words.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ זִקְנֵֽי־ גִלְעָ֖ד אֶל־ יִפְתָּ֑ח יְהוָ֗ה יִהְיֶ֤ה שֹׁמֵ֙עַ֙ בֵּֽינוֹתֵ֔ינוּ אִם־ לֹ֥א כִדְבָרְךָ֖ כֵּ֥ן נַעֲשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him their leader and commander. And Jephthah repeated all his terms in the presence of the LORD at Mizpah.
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a man chosen to lead Israel in a time of trouble.
The elders of Gilead asked Jephthah to help them.
Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead.
The people of Gilead made Jephthah their leader.
They also made him their commander.
Jephthah spoke all his words before the LORD.
He did this at Mizpah.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ יִפְתָּח֙ עִם־ זִקְנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֔ד וַיָּשִׂ֨ימוּ הָעָ֥ם אוֹת֛וֹ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לְרֹ֣אשׁ וּלְקָצִ֑ין וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר יִפְתָּ֧ח אֶת־ כָּל־ דְּבָרָ֛יו לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בַּמִּצְפָּֽה׃פ

passages.text: Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites, saying, “What do you have against me that you have come to fight against my land?”
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a leader of Gilead.
Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites.
Jephthah asked the king a question.
Jephthah said, “Why have you come to fight against my land?”
Jephthah wanted to know what the king had against him.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִפְתָּח֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־ מֶ֥לֶךְ בְּנֵֽי־ עַמּ֖וֹן לֵאמֹ֑ר מַה־ לִּ֣י וָלָ֔ךְ כִּֽי־ בָ֥אתָ אֵלַ֖י לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם בְּאַרְצִֽי׃

passages.text: The king of the Ammonites answered Jephthah’s messengers, “When Israel came up out of Egypt, they seized my land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and all the way to the Jordan. Now, therefore, restore it peaceably.”
passages.sermon:
The king of the Ammonites spoke to Jephthah’s messengers.
He said Israel took my land.
This happened when Israel came up from Egypt.
They took the land from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River.
They also took the land up to the Jordan River.
Now return these lands to me in peace.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בְּנֵי־ עַמּ֜וֹן אֶל־ מַלְאֲכֵ֣י יִפְתָּ֗ח כִּֽי־ לָקַ֨ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶת־ אַרְצִי֙ בַּעֲלוֹת֣וֹ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם מֵאַרְנ֥וֹן וְעַד־ הַיַּבֹּ֖ק וְעַד־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וְעַתָּ֕ה הָשִׁ֥יבָה אֶתְהֶ֖ן בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Jephthah again sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites to tell him, “This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take away the land of Moab or of the Ammonites.
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a leader of Israel.
Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites.
Jephthah sent these messengers again.
Jephthah gave them a message for the king.
Jephthah said, “Israel did not take the land of Moab.
Israel did not take the land of the Ammonites.”
passages.original: וַיּ֥וֹסֶף ע֖וֹד יִפְתָּ֑ח וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־ מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יִפְתָּ֑ח לֹֽא־ לָקַ֤ח יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־ אֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב וְאֶת־ אֶ֖רֶץ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: But when Israel came up out of Egypt, they traveled through the wilderness to the Red Sea and came to Kadesh.
passages.sermon:
Israel was a people whom God brought out of Egypt.
Israel left Egypt.
Israel traveled through the wilderness.
Israel journeyed until they reached the Red Sea.
Israel then came to a place called Kadesh.
passages.original: כִּ֖י בַּעֲלוֹתָ֣ם מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ עַד־ יַם־ ס֔וּף וַיָּבֹ֖א קָדֵֽשָׁה׃

passages.text: Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Please let us pass through your land,’ but the king of Edom would not listen. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he would not consent. So Israel stayed in Kadesh.
passages.sermon:
Israel was a nation led by God.
Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom.
The messengers said, “Please let us pass through your land.”
The king of Edom did not listen.
Israel also sent messengers to the king of Moab.
The king of Moab did not agree.
Israel stayed in Kadesh.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מַלְאָכִ֣ים׀ אֶל־ מֶלֶךְ֩ אֱד֨וֹם׀ לֵאמֹ֜ר אֶעְבְּרָה־ נָּ֣א בְאַרְצֶ֗ךָ וְלֹ֤א שָׁמַע֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֱד֔וֹם וְגַ֨ם אֶל־ מֶ֧לֶךְ מוֹאָ֛ב שָׁלַ֖ח וְלֹ֣א אָבָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּקָדֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: Then Israel traveled through the wilderness and bypassed the lands of Edom and Moab. They came to the east side of the land of Moab and camped on the other side of the Arnon. But they did not enter the territory of Moab, since the Arnon was its border.
passages.sermon:
Israel was a people whom God brought out of Egypt.
Israel traveled through the wilderness.
Israel did not go through the land of Edom.
Israel did not go through the land of Moab.
Israel went around Edom and Moab.
Israel came to the east side of the land of Moab.
Israel camped on the other side of the Arnon River.
Israel did not enter the territory of Moab.
The Arnon River was the border of Moab.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר וַיָּ֜סָב אֶת־ אֶ֤רֶץ אֱדוֹם֙ וְאֶת־ אֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב וַיָּבֹ֤א מִמִּזְרַח־ שֶׁ֙מֶשׁ֙ לְאֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּן בְּעֵ֣בֶר אַרְנ֑וֹן וְלֹא־ בָ֙אוּ֙ בִּגְב֣וּל מוֹאָ֔ב כִּ֥י אַרְנ֖וֹן גְּב֥וּל מוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: And Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and said to him, ‘Please let us pass through your land into our own place.’
passages.sermon:
Israel was a nation led by God.
Sihon was king of the Amorites.
Sihon ruled in the city of Heshbon.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon.
The messengers spoke to Sihon.
They said, “Please let us pass through your land.”
They said, “We want to go to our own place.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־ סִיח֥וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ־ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נַעְבְּרָה־ נָּ֥א בְאַרְצְךָ֖ עַד־ מְקוֹמִֽי׃

passages.text: But Sihon would not trust Israel to pass through his territory. So he gathered all his people, encamped in Jahaz, and fought with Israel.
passages.sermon:
Sihon was the king of the Amorites.
He ruled in Heshbon.
Israel asked Sihon for permission to pass through his land.
Sihon did not trust Israel.
He refused to let Israel pass through his territory.
Sihon gathered all his people.
They camped at Jahaz.
Sihon and his people fought against Israel.
passages.original: וְלֹא־ הֶאֱמִ֨ין סִיח֤וֹן אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עֲבֹ֣ר בִּגְבֻל֔וֹ וַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף סִיחוֹן֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ עַמּ֔וֹ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּיָ֑הְצָה וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם עִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Then the LORD, the God of Israel, delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, who defeated them. So Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites who inhabited that country, seizing all the land from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD gave Sihon and all his people into Israel’s hand.
Israel defeated Sihon and his people.
Israel took all the land of the Amorites.
The Amorites lived in that land.
Israel took all the territory of the Amorites.
This land stretched from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River.
It also reached from the wilderness to the Jordan River.
passages.original: וַ֠יִּתֵּן יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־ סִיח֧וֹן וְאֶת־ כָּל־ עַמּ֛וֹ בְּיַ֥ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיַּכּ֑וּם וַיִּירַשׁ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֚ת כָּל־ אֶ֣רֶץ הָאֱמֹרִ֔י יוֹשֵׁ֖ב הָאָ֥רֶץ הַהִֽיא׃ וַיִּ֣ירְשׁ֔וּ אֵ֖ת כָּל־ גְּב֣וּל הָאֱמֹרִ֑י מֵֽאַרְנוֹן֙ וְעַד־ הַיַּבֹּ֔ק וּמִן־ הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְעַד־ הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

passages.text: Now since the LORD, the God of Israel, has driven out the Amorites from before His people Israel, should you now possess it?
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD drove out the Amorites.
He removed them from before His people Israel.
You are not part of Israel.
Should you now take possession of their land?
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֞ה יְהוָ֣ה׀ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הוֹרִישׁ֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י מִפְּנֵ֖י עַמּ֣וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּירָשֶֽׁנּוּ׃

passages.text: Do you not possess whatever your god Chemosh grants you? So also, we possess whatever the LORD our God has granted us.
passages.sermon:
Chemosh is your god.
You possess whatever Chemosh gives you.
The LORD is our God.
We possess whatever the LORD our God gives us.
passages.original: הֲלֹ֞א אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר יוֹרִֽישְׁךָ֛ כְּמ֥וֹשׁ אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אוֹת֥וֹ תִירָ֑שׁ וְאֵת֩ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹרִ֜ישׁ יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ מִפָּנֵ֖ינוּ אוֹת֥וֹ נִירָֽשׁ׃

passages.text: Are you now so much better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever contend with Israel or fight against them?
passages.sermon:
Balak was the son of Zippor.
Balak was king of Moab.
You are not greater than Balak.
Balak did not argue with Israel.
Balak did not fight against Israel.
You should not think you are better than Balak.
You should not fight against Israel.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה הֲט֥וֹב טוֹב֙ אַתָּ֔ה מִבָּלָ֥ק בֶּן־ צִפּ֖וֹר מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֑ב הֲר֥וֹב רָב֙ עִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִם־ נִלְחֹ֥ם נִלְחַ֖ם בָּֽם׃

passages.text: For three hundred years Israel has lived in Heshbon, Aroer, and their villages, as well as all the cities along the banks of the Arnon. Why did you not take them back during that time?
passages.sermon:
Israel lived in Heshbon for three hundred years.
Israel lived in the villages of Heshbon for three hundred years.
Israel lived in Aroer for three hundred years.
Israel lived in the villages of Aroer for three hundred years.
Israel lived in all the cities along the banks of the Arnon for three hundred years.
You did not take these places back during that time.
Why did you not take them back then?
passages.original: בְּשֶׁ֣בֶת יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל בְּחֶשְׁבּ֨וֹן וּבִבְנוֹתֶ֜יהָ וּבְעַרְע֣וֹר וּבִבְנוֹתֶ֗יהָ וּבְכָל־ הֶֽעָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־ יְדֵ֣י אַרְנ֔וֹן שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וּמַדּ֥וּעַ לֹֽא־ הִצַּלְתֶּ֖ם בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽיא׃

passages.text: I have not sinned against you, but you have done me wrong by waging war against me. May the LORD, the Judge, decide today between the Israelites and the Ammonites.”
passages.sermon:
Jephthah spoke to the king of the Ammonites.
Jephthah said, “I have not sinned against you.
You have done wrong to me.
You fight against me.
The LORD is the Judge.
May the LORD decide today.
Let Him judge between the Israelites and the Ammonites.”
passages.original: וְאָֽנֹכִי֙ לֹֽא־ חָטָ֣אתִי לָ֔ךְ וְאַתָּ֞ה עֹשֶׂ֥ה אִתִּ֛י רָעָ֖ה לְהִלָּ֣חֶם בִּ֑י יִשְׁפֹּ֨ט יְהוָ֤ה הַשֹּׁפֵט֙ הַיּ֔וֹם בֵּ֚ין בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּבֵ֖ין בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: But the king of the Ammonites paid no heed to the message Jephthah sent him.
passages.sermon:
The king of the Ammonites heard Jephthah’s message.
Jephthah sent this message to him.
The king did not listen.
The king ignored Jephthah’s words.
passages.original: וְלֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔ע מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן אֶל־ דִּבְרֵ֣י יִפְתָּ֔ח אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁלַ֖ח אֵלָֽיו׃פ

passages.text: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, then through Mizpah of Gilead. And from there he advanced against the Ammonites.
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a leader of Israel.
The Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah.
Jephthah traveled through Gilead.
He traveled through Manasseh.
He went through Mizpah of Gilead.
Jephthah left Mizpah of Gilead.
He advanced against the Ammonites.
passages.original: וַתְּהִ֤י עַל־ יִפְתָּח֙ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּעֲבֹ֥ר אֶת־ הַגִּלְעָ֖ד וְאֶת־ מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַֽיַּעֲבֹר֙ אֶת־ מִצְפֵּ֣ה גִלְעָ֔ד וּמִמִּצְפֵּ֣ה גִלְעָ֔ד עָבַ֖ר בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Jephthah made this vow to the LORD: “If indeed You will deliver the Ammonites into my hand, then whatever comes out the door of my house to greet me on my triumphant return from the Ammonites will belong to the LORD, and I will offer it up as a burnt offering.”
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a leader of Israel.
He made a vow to the LORD.
He said, “If You, LORD, give the Ammonites into my hand,
then whoever comes out of the door of my house to meet me
when I return safely from the Ammonites
will belong to the LORD.
I will offer that one as a burnt offering.”
passages.original: וַיִּדַּ֨ר יִפְתָּ֥ח נֶ֛דֶר לַיהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אִם־ נָת֥וֹן תִּתֵּ֛ן אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן בְּיָדִֽי׃ וְהָיָ֣ה הַיּוֹצֵ֗א אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֵצֵ֜א מִדַּלְתֵ֤י בֵיתִי֙ לִקְרָאתִ֔י בְּשׁוּבִ֥י בְשָׁל֖וֹם מִבְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן וְהָיָה֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְהַעֲלִיתִ֖הוּ עוֹלָֽה׃פ

passages.text: So Jephthah crossed over to the Ammonites to fight against them, and the LORD delivered them into his hand.
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a leader of Israel.
Jephthah went to the Ammonites.
He went to fight against the Ammonites.
The LORD gave the Ammonites into Jephthah’s hand.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲבֹ֥ר יִפְתָּ֛ח אֶל־ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן לְהִלָּ֣חֶם בָּ֑ם וַיִתְּנֵ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: With a great blow he devastated twenty cities from Aroer to the vicinity of Minnith, as far as Abel-keramim. So the Ammonites were subdued before the Israelites.
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a leader of Israel.
Jephthah fought against the Ammonites.
Jephthah struck the Ammonites with a very great blow.
He destroyed twenty cities.
He attacked from Aroer to the area near Minnith.
He continued as far as Abel-keramim.
The Ammonites became subdued.
The Israelites defeated the Ammonites.
passages.original: וַיַּכֵּ֡ם מֵעֲרוֹעֵר֩ וְעַד־ בּוֹאֲךָ֨ מִנִּ֜ית עֶשְׂרִ֣ים עִ֗יר וְעַד֙ אָבֵ֣ל כְּרָמִ֔ים מַכָּ֖ה גְּדוֹלָ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וַיִּכָּֽנְעוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: And when Jephthah returned home to Mizpah, there was his daughter coming out to meet him with tambourines and dancing! She was his only child; he had no son or daughter besides her.
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a leader of Israel.
He returned home to Mizpah.
He went to his house.
His daughter came out to meet him.
She played tambourines.
She danced.
She was his only child.
Jephthah had no other son.
Jephthah had no other daughter.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א יִפְתָּ֣ח הַמִּצְפָּה֮ אֶל־ בֵּיתוֹ֒ וְהִנֵּ֤ה בִתּוֹ֙ יֹצֵ֣את לִקְרָאת֔וֹ בְתֻפִּ֖ים וּבִמְחֹל֑וֹת וְרַק֙ הִ֣יא יְחִידָ֔ה אֵֽין־ ל֥וֹ מִמֶּ֛נּוּ בֵּ֖ן אוֹ־ בַֽת׃

passages.text: As soon as Jephthah saw her, he tore his clothes and said, “No! Not my daughter! You have brought me to my knees! You have brought great misery upon me, for I have given my word to the LORD and cannot take it back.”
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a leader of Israel.
He had just returned home after defeating the Ammonites.
Jephthah saw his daughter coming out to meet him.
She was his only child.
When Jephthah saw her, he tore his clothes.
He said, "No! My daughter!"
"You have brought me to my knees."
"You have brought great misery upon me."
"I have given my word to the LORD."
"I cannot take it back."
passages.original: וַיְהִי֩ כִרְאוֹת֨וֹ אוֹתָ֜הּ וַיִּקְרַ֣ע אֶת־ בְּגָדָ֗יו וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֲהָ֤הּ בִּתִּי֙ הַכְרֵ֣עַ הִכְרַעְתִּ֔נִי וְאַ֖תְּ הָיִ֣יתְ בְּעֹֽכְרָ֑י וְאָנֹכִ֗י פָּצִ֤יתִי־ פִי֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א אוּכַ֖ל לָשֽׁוּב׃

passages.text: “My father,” she replied, “you have given your word to the LORD. Do to me as you have said, for the LORD has avenged you of your enemies, the Ammonites.”
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a judge of Israel.
Jephthah had only one child, a daughter.
Jephthah made a vow to the LORD.
Jephthah’s daughter spoke to him.
She said, “My father, you have given your word to the LORD.”
She said, “Do to me as you have said.”
She said, “The LORD has given you victory over your enemies.”
She said, “The LORD has defeated the Ammonites for you.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו אָבִי֙ פָּצִ֤יתָה אֶת־ פִּ֙יךָ֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה עֲשֵׂ֣ה לִ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר יָצָ֣א מִפִּ֑יךָ אַחֲרֵ֡י אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂה֩ לְךָ֙ יְהוָ֧ה נְקָמ֛וֹת מֵאֹיְבֶ֖יךָ מִבְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: She also said to her father, “Let me do this one thing: Let me wander for two months through the mountains with my friends and mourn my virginity.”
passages.sermon:
Jephthah’s daughter spoke to her father.
She said, “Let me have this request.
Allow me two months.
I will go to the mountains.
I will go with my friends.
I will mourn that I will never marry.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ אָבִ֔יהָ יֵעָ֥שֶׂה לִּ֖י הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה הַרְפֵּ֨ה מִמֶּ֜נִּי שְׁנַ֣יִם חֳדָשִׁ֗ים וְאֵֽלְכָה֙ וְיָרַדְתִּ֣י עַל־ הֶֽהָרִ֔ים וְאֶבְכֶּה֙ עַל־ בְּתוּלַ֔י אָנֹכִ֖י וְרֵעְיֹתָי׃

passages.text: “Go,” he said. And he sent her away for two months. So she left with her friends and mourned her virginity upon the mountains.
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a judge of Israel.
Jephthah was the father of the young woman.
Jephthah spoke to his daughter.
Jephthah said, “Go.”
Jephthah sent his daughter away for two months.
Jephthah’s daughter left.
Her friends went with her.
She mourned her virginity.
She mourned on the mountains.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לֵ֔כִי וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח אוֹתָ֖הּ שְׁנֵ֣י חֳדָשִׁ֑ים וַתֵּ֤לֶךְ הִיא֙ וְרֵ֣עוֹתֶ֔יהָ וַתֵּ֥בְךְּ עַל־ בְּתוּלֶ֖יהָ עַל־ הֶהָרִֽים׃

passages.text: After two months, she returned to her father, and he did to her as he had vowed. And she had never had relations with a man. So it has become a custom in Israel that each year the young women of Israel go out for four days to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite.
passages.sermon:
Jephthah was a leader in Israel.
Jephthah had made a vow to God.
Jephthah had a daughter.
After two months, Jephthah’s daughter returned to her father.
Jephthah did to his daughter as he had vowed.
Jephthah’s daughter had never been with a man.
This event became a custom in Israel.
Each year, the young women of Israel go out for four days.
They lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י מִקֵּ֣ץ׀ שְׁנַ֣יִם חֳדָשִׁ֗ים וַתָּ֙שָׁב֙ אֶל־ אָבִ֔יהָ וַיַּ֣עַשׂ לָ֔הּ אֶת־ נִדְר֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָדָ֑ר וְהִיא֙ לֹא־ יָדְעָ֣ה אִ֔ישׁ וַתְּהִי־ חֹ֖ק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ מִיָּמִ֣ים׀ יָמִ֗ימָה תֵּלַ֙כְנָה֙ בְּנ֣וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְתַנּ֕וֹת לְבַת־ יִפְתָּ֖ח הַגִּלְעָדִ֑י אַרְבַּ֥עַת יָמִ֖ים בַּשָּׁנָֽה׃ס
